title: El hijo del Cóndor · Aprender la salida
palette: Charcoal and slate folded-paper cave, ochre earth, dusty sage vegetation, ivory and clay garments. Pale dawn for freedom; warm indirect ochre light underground, never neon. Same matte paper material across daylight, dark chambers and dusk.
shared_scene_continuity: Todas las superficies y seres de papel recortado, incluidas caras, animales, herramientas y suelo. Inmersión completa sin base exterior de maqueta.
La cueva alta de Juramía tiene una piedra de cierre; la de Jujía desciende por corredores abiertos. No confundir lugares ni poner al cóndor en el ciclo subterráneo.
Sólo aparece el reparto de cada toma. Rostros pequeños planos; vestuario completo de continuidad editorial. No importar lluvia germinante de Creación ni noches domésticas de Arámai.
continuity_rules: José Juan permanece humano y adulto desde su primera aparición; el crecimiento se recuerda por sombra, no metamorfosis en ave.
Madre arcilla y trenza única; José Juan camisa marfil/pantalón arena; Jujía gris/carbón; dos peones diferenciados por túnica; mujeres no son trofeos.
Violencia y cautiverio narrados sin representar agresión, cuerpos heridos, sangre, sexualidad o ataduras sobre personas.
El cierre sigue al relato publicado, sin presentar a la hija como esposa histórica de Chaves. No hay boda ni contacto romántico.

narrative.source_locator: Chaves1946 secciónXV pp327–331/PDF23–27, José Jusayú por Roberto Iguarán; relectura2026-09-07.
narrative.nature: Adaptación audiovisual de la página vigente, contrastada con su fuente histórica; no nueva edición documental ni publicación integral.
narrative.chosen_variant: Texto público comprimido; registra diferencia del final: Chaves da unión con Jujía, página residencia junto a la hija. No representar boda ni fundirlas.
narrative.visual_license: Sombra de infancia, piedra y senderos que se pliegan, sombras que se levantan son traducciones plásticas editoriales; no símbolos tradicionales ni episodios nuevos.

events.source: Public mito paragraphs1–2; Chaves XV pp327–328.
events.action: Juramía encerró a una joven en una cueva alta. Allí nació su hijo y creció con rapidez. La madre seguía buscando una salida.

events.source: Public paragraphs2–3 and closing; Chaves XV p328. Order of crossing is staging, not new traditional detail.
events.action: El muchacho observó la piedra hasta descubrir cómo abrirla. Cuando el cóndor salió, sostuvo la puerta. Su madre cruzó primero; él salió detrás.
Llegaron a una ranchería. El hijo recibió el nombre de José Juan. Trabajaron para sostenerse; después, él abrió una roza y contrató dos peones.

events.source: Public paragraph4; Chaves XV p329. Attacks and injuries off screen, no mutilation imagery.
events.action: Jujía apareció junto al fogón, devoró la comida y atacó a los peones. José Juan se enfrentó a ella. La siguió hasta otra cueva.

events.source: Public paragraph5; Chaves XV pp329–330. Compresses repeated bargains as public version; women not prizes.
events.action: Serpientes guardaban la entrada. Jujía ofreció una alianza y dejó salir a dos jóvenes alijuna. Pero los peones traicionaron a José Juan y lo abandonaron.

events.source: Public paragraphs5–6; Chaves XV p330. Free standing figure plus cut rope is nonviolent ellipsis of being left tied.
events.action: La soga quedó cortada. Solo entre corredores subterráneos, José Juan no encontró la salida. Jujía regresó, lo liberó y le mostró el camino de vuelta.

events.source: Public paragraph6 and editorial reflection; Chaves XV p330. Killing wholly off image; resurrection shown by nonviolent material metaphor.
events.action: José Juan alcanzó a los traidores y los mató. Después les devolvió la vida. El daño no desapareció: la restitución detuvo una nueva persecución.

events.source: Public paragraph7; Chaves XV pp330–331. No blows or force visible; don't import Kosina's speaking horse.
events.action: Volvió donde Jujía. Faltaba una prueba: dominar un caballo difícil. José Juan sostuvo el lazo, esperó y logró montarlo. Esta vez pudo seguir adelante.

events.source: Public paragraphs8–9; published editorial expansion for final daughter relation, distinct from Chaves's Jujia ending. No marriage staged.
events.action: Entró al dominio subterráneo sin ser prisionero. Allí permaneció junto a la hija de Jujía y los animales. No volvió a buscar al cóndor.

events.source: Public paragraphs9–11; independent maternal ending is published editorial emphasis. No extra reunion.
events.action: Su madre conservó una vida propia en la ranchería. Todo había empezado al observar una puerta: un hijo encontró cómo abrirla, y los dos pudieron salir.

story_thesis: La salida compartida inaugura una autonomía que las pruebas, la violencia y la reparación vuelven más compleja, no una victoria limpia.

inventory.desc: Juramía, mythical bird called condor: broad BLACK cut-paper wings with narrow ivory feather bands and ivory NECK RUFF, small bare dusky-red head, pale hooked beak; normal bird anatomy. Not white-headed eagle, giant monster, humanoid or transformed José Juan.

José Juan's adult mother: small flat side-profile, warm brown paper face with contour-only nose, long black braid; plain clay-terracotta ankle-length Wayuu manta over ivory underlayer, simple sandals. Complete opaque clothing, no ornaments, headwear or paint. Adult, not a bride or prize.

José Juan: young ADULT human, short irregular black cut-paper hair, warm brown flat profile, tiny cut eye, slender ordinary adult proportions, plain ivory long-sleeved shirt and SAND ankle trousers, dark plain sandals. NO cape, wings, feathers, beard, hat, muscular torso or sculpted head.

Jujía: older adult woman with gray hair in two LOW loose sections, plain layered charcoal and dark brown ankle-length manta over sand underlayer, simple dark sandals. Flat paper side-profile with minimal line for eye; not crone caricature, young seductress, monster or witch costume. No injuries visible.

First adult hired worker: tall slim human with short black hair, full plain cream knee-length working tunic over sand trousers, simple sandals; flat paper profile. Distinguishable from Jose by long tunic, not shirt.

Second adult hired worker: slightly shorter stocky human with short wavy dark hair, full rust-brown knee-length tunic over brown trousers and simple sandals; flat cut-paper profile, no facial caricature.
Adult alijuna woman: long muted slate-blue plain dress, dark thin sash, dark hair pinned low, flat side profile. Walks independently, never carried, handed over, sexualized or posed as a trophy.
Adult alijuna woman: sand plain ankle-length dress, single dark braid, no ornaments, flat cut-paper face. Distinct from the blue-dressed woman, independent posture.

Adult daughter of Jujía: long loose straight black cut-paper hair, plain sand ankle-length dress with CHARCOAL diagonal sash and narrow clay strip; flat side profile. Separate self-directed posture, not bridal, no romantic contact or trophy composition.

One ordinary dark CHESTNUT horse, black paper mane, tail and lower legs; four correct legs. Almost flat layered cut-paper silhouette with a few folded pieces, NO realistic muscles, fur or glass eyes. Plain rope bridle, no saddle ornament, wing, horn or armor.

Exactly TWO separate slender paper snakes guarding opposite sides of a natural cave: charcoal and muted earth brown, flat cut silhouettes and broad overlapping scales, mouths closed, bodies visible and not tangled; no giant monster, attack or wound.

Juramía's high cave: asymmetric charcoal/ochre stacked-paper cliffs, a SINGLE broad dark movable stone slab at its mouth, huge interior, small pale dawn seam. Not masonry, palace, frame, scenic miniature base or known named mountain.

Jujía's subterranean domain: immense connected natural corridors of folded slate/ochre paper, traversable winding ground and distant warm opening. Distinct from Juramía's high cave: downward branching passages, no mechanical door, jewels, palace or archaeological cutaway.

Small worked clearing with broad cut-paper EARTH FURROWS, cut shrub stems and limited dry green leaves, irregular twig fence made of flat paper strips; no lush crop fields or real dirt. Tools only if declared.

Modest dispersed ranchería: plain ochre cut-paper dwelling with dark OPEN doorway and adjacent palm-sheet shade roof, thin flat-paper posts, immense dryland around. Domestic, no ceremonial props, no detailed fabricated clan designs.

Guajira dryland in broad overlapping ochre matte paper sheets, muted sage cut-leaf thorn shrubs and cardon-like vertical cut silhouettes; distant layered ridges without claiming an exact geographic cave.
Small plain ivory garment patch and a single slender thorn used for repair, represented by simple paper cutouts, not bloody, not piercing skin; mother's clothes remain complete.

Low hearth of folded charcoal paper stones with small amber cut-paper flame; modest terracotta-colored PAPER cooking pot and three bowls with clearly thin overlapping assembled rims, simple broad cut-paper food shapes. Not smooth ceramic or metal.
Two resting agricultural hoes assembled from flat brown paper shafts and folded gray paper blades, used only as field tools; never raised as weapons.
Plain light-beige narrow folded-paper cord. Broken upper end and loose coil can indicate abandonment; NO person tied up, neck loop, binding or violence visible.
Plain matte beige folded-paper rope for the horse test: held low with a loose curve, or coil on ground; no whip, blows, tight neck loop or forceful struggle.

reference_review.method: Inspección directa de los tres trípticos y modelos de identidades, caballo, serpientes, roza y dominio; conservar identidad pero aplanar caras, animales y material realista.
decisions: No copiar facetas escultóricas, tierra granular o piedra realista de fichas anteriores.
Retener lógica de puerta y descenso de trípticos, ampliar todo el ciclo narrativo sin rehacerlos.
Sin subir ninguna referencia local al generador.

blocks.voice_over: Volvió donde Jujía. Faltaba una prueba: dominar un caballo difícil. José Juan sostuvo el lazo, esperó y logró montarlo. Esta vez pudo seguir adelante.
blocks.voice_provenance: Public paragraph7; Chaves XV pp330–331. No blows or force visible; don't import Kosina's speaking horse.
blocks.delivery: Voz externa sobria con silencios entre ciclos; sin sincronía labial.

keyframes.title: Antes de acercarse
keyframes.visual: Very wide outdoor paper clearing beside low cave. Jose stands to the side of ONE dark chestnut horse, at safe visible distance, holding a plain beige paper rope low in a loose curve; horse stands alert four feet grounded, ears attentive, no rearing or struggle. Both entire and small, combined max25% canvas height. Full landscape has angular olive paper shrubs, broad ochre ground sheets and natural folded rock. No spectator Jujia, whip, weapon, saddle decoration or fantasy anatomy.

keyframes.title: La prueba abre un paso
keyframes.visual: Very wide view inside the beginning of a descending cave. Tiny Jose RIDES one ordinary chestnut horse calmly, both together max23% canvas height. The front hoof rests DIRECTLY on a continuous broad ochre ground layer that folds down in three connected strips, following the horse's path into a warm lower corridor. The path remains one supported geological route, not a floating magic carpet. Side-profile almost-flat horse and rider, four legs and plain slack rope bridle. No other people or animals, no combat, no sword, no wings. Every cliff and mane clearly PAPER.

keyframes.title: Habitar sin cautiverio
keyframes.visual: Very wide interior natural chamber with TWO separate walkable routes. Jose stands on one path at mid distance and adult daughter of Jujia walks on the other further away, looking toward her own route, no eye contact or touching. One chestnut horse rests nearby Jose. All small complete cut-paper silhouettes, daughter sand dress with charcoal/clay diagonal sash and long loose hair. Huge layered charcoal and ochre cave surrounds viewer, multiple open passages, warm reflected daylight from high fissure. No Jujia, mother, throne, wedding, closed door or trophy staging.

keyframes.title: La vida de ella
keyframes.visual: Wide morning domestic view of the same ranchería. ONLY mother, terracotta manta over ivory underlayer and single black braid, sits completely visible in the shade mending a plain ivory garment patch. Her home's wide open doorway leads straight onto the dryland path; the roof and every post are clearly folded PAPER not real thatch/wood. Ordinary quiet agency, no sad waiting gaze, son, baby, condor, ritual objects or loom. Scene rich in paper overlaps, shade bands, small sage shrubs and distant ridges.

keyframes.title: Salir por voluntad propia
keyframes.visual: Very wide exterior of the same modest paper home at clear morning. Mother walks freely away from its OPEN doorway onto a broad layered ochre path, full body small in middle distance. Match the terracotta manta, ivory hem and one black braid. Ending emphasizes her own movement and unblocked horizon, not lonely abandonment.
